players.product: wafer-level burn-in systems (FOX) with WaferPak full-wafer contactors, and Sonoma package-level burn-in, for AI accelerators and silicon photonics

quarterly_data.signal: CFO Chris Siu: third quarter revenue of $10.3 million was down 44% from $18.3 million a year earlier, driven by lower shipments of FOX systems and WaferPaks for wafer-level burn-in, partially offset by stronger demand for Sonoma systems and BIMs from the hyperscale customer. Contactor revenue (WaferPaks, BIMs, BIPs) totaled $3 million, 29% of revenue; non-GAAP gross margin was 36.5% vs 42.7% a year ago on lower volume and less WaferPak mix.
quarterly_data.figure: $10.3 million revenue (down 44% from $18.3 million); contactors $3 million (29%); non-GAAP gross margin 36.5% vs 42.7%

quarterly_data.signal: Bookings and record effective backlog: Q3 bookings were $37.2 million vs $6.2 million in Q2 (orders for FOX systems, WaferPaks and auto-aligners for AI, silicon photonics and silicon carbide), book-to-bill exceeding 3.5x. Quarter-end backlog was $38.7 million; a further $12.2 million was booked in the first 5 weeks of Q4, taking effective backlog to a record $50.9 million.
quarterly_data.figure: Q3 bookings $37.2 million (vs $6.2 million); backlog $38.7 million; effective backlog $50.9 million; book-to-bill exceeding 3.5x

quarterly_data.signal: Guidance: full-year fiscal 2026 (ending May 29, 2026) revenue expected on the high side of the $45 million to $50 million range, second-half bookings on the high side of the $60 million to $80 million range, non-GAAP net loss per diluted share between negative $0.13 and negative $0.09, and a return to non-GAAP profitability in the fourth quarter; management expects 'significant revenue growth in fiscal '27'.
quarterly_data.figure: FY2026 revenue high side of $45 million to $50 million; 2H bookings high side of $60 million to $80 million; non-GAAP EPS negative $0.13 to negative $0.09

quarterly_data.signal: AI wafer-level burn-in: Aehr received a $14 million follow-on production order from its lead wafer-level AI accelerator processor customer (not named) for multiple fully automated FOX-XP systems, each testing nine 300-millimeter wafers in parallel, with WaferPak contactors and integrated auto-aligners, plus aligners to upgrade the existing FOX-XP installed base to full automation, for data center training and inference.
quarterly_data.figure: $14 million follow-on order; nine 300-millimeter wafers in parallel per system

quarterly_data.signal: The wafer-level benchmark with a top-tier AI processor supplier (not named) is 'taking longer than we originally expected' because of 'a technical misunderstanding on the clock configurations'; Aehr is taking device data with the current WaferPak and redesigning WaferPaks, with more data over the next several months. Management cites significant interest in wafer-level burn-in of dies headed into advanced packages such as TSMC's CoWoS with HBM DRAM stacks and transceiver chipsets, since screening before packaging avoids throwing away the whole multichip package.

Package-level hyperscale customer (a premier large-scale data center provider, not named) selected Aehr for production burn-in of its next-generation, significantly higher-power AI ASIC with an initial Sonoma production order; that ASIC is expected to move to production later this year at even higher volumes than the current device. Aehr expects a significant near-term follow-on order for the current device, and the customer is forecasting a substantial expansion of Sonoma purchases beginning in the second half of calendar 2026 and continuing into '27, with overlapping ramps. The customer has asked about DFT for a third device to consider wafer-level burn-in on FOX.
quarterly_data.figure: Sonoma expansion forecast beginning second half of calendar 2026 into '27

quarterly_data.signal: Memory: Aehr achieved the correlation a key memory supplier asked for and is discussing system specs for its next-generation flash and high bandwidth flash; it hopes to close in the next few months on a development agreement, followed by a 12- to 18-month development of memory-optimized blades for FOX-XP/NP. It is also in discussions with other memory suppliers that produce HBM (CEO sees 'interesting challenges' in HBM 4E suited to wafer-level burn-in); management believes memory 'could drive orders in fiscal '27 with ramps in fiscal '28'.
quarterly_data.figure: 12- to 18-month development; orders possible in fiscal '27, ramps in fiscal '28

quarterly_data.signal: Capacity: in addition to the Fremont expansion (about a 20 system per month footprint), Aehr begins shipping Sonoma systems this quarter from a contract manufacturer (actually two working together), 'adding capacity of more than 20 additional Sonoma systems per month', aimed to be ready by late summer when the Sonoma ramp hits; all FOX products stay in Fremont.
quarterly_data.figure: more than 20 additional Sonoma systems per month

quarterly_data.signal: Market sizing: CEO says TAMs are 'multi-hundreds of millions of dollars for package-level burn-in' and higher for wafer-level, with total burn-in spend 'probably ... measured in multiple billions of dollars per year in the next couple of years'; he estimates most ASICs are not burned in today ('I don't know if it's 20%, maybe it's 5%') and maybe half of AI accelerators are, with rising power per generation breaking existing tools. Consumables were light this year (an outlier); long term they should be 30% or more of total revenue.
quarterly_data.figure: consumables expected at 30% or more of revenue long term

quarterly_data.signal: Power semiconductors: Aehr is working with its lead GaN production customer on many new devices (automotive, intermediate bus conversion, data center, electrical infrastructure), won a new silicon carbide customer in Taiwan (small FOX-XP system for qualification and production), and sees an uptick in silicon carbide forecasts but is not yet counting on significant revenue from that segment.

players.product: burn-in and reliability screening for optical devices — data-center transceivers, chip-to-chip I/O and silicon photonics (FOX wafer-level and Sonoma package-level)

quarterly_data.signal: Major new silicon photonics customer (not named), developing silicon photonics transceivers for data center networking and optical I/O, placed an initial order for multiple high-power FOX-XP (nine-wafer) and FOX-NP wafer-level burn-in systems plus auto-aligner and WaferPak sets, all scheduled to ship in the fiscal fourth quarter ending May 29, '26; it has forecast multiple additional XP production systems over the next year. This win primarily drove the $12.2 million booked in the first 5 weeks of Q4.
quarterly_data.figure: $12.2 million bookings in first 5 weeks of Q4, driven primarily by this customer

quarterly_data.signal: Lead silicon photonics customer (not named) placed a follow-on order for a new high-power FOX-XP system and an upgrade of an existing system to the latest high-power fully automated configuration; Aehr integrated its systems with the customer's autonomous-guided robots for lights-out operation, and the customer forecast additional production systems as it ramps into next calendar year. Management calls Aehr the market leader in wafer-level burn-in for silicon photonics transceivers, used to stabilize laser diode emitters and catch early-life failures before packaging.
